title: The J-2 property passes from an affine open cover to every affine open
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], and let $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an affine open covering. If every ring $\mathcal O_X(U_i)$ is J-2, then for every affine open $V\subseteq X$ the ring $\mathcal O_X(V)$ is J-2. Here J-2 is the ring predicate of [def-exc-excellent-ring]: the regular locus of every finite type algebra over the ring is open.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), implication (4) implies (3). The S in the printed covering formula in (4) denotes the scheme X of the lemma.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq X$ and put $R=\mathcal O_X(V)$. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], $R$ is Noetherian. Let $R\to B$ be any finite type algebra and put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Under the affine identification $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, its structure morphism is $h=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to B)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion]: for every point of $Y$, take the whole affine $Y$ as its source neighbourhood and the whole affine $V$ as the target neighbourhood. The resulting ring map on global sections is exactly the given finite type map $R\to B$. Thus $h:Y\to V$ is locally of finite type. This also covers $B=0$, where the pointwise condition is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), (4) implies (1) followed by (1) implies (3), specialized to the finite type algebra B over an affine open V; Tags 01T1 (definition-finite-type) and 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); Properties Tag 01OW (properties.tex, lemma-locally-Noetherian).

proof.text: The inclusion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. It is an immersion: factor it as the identity of $V$ followed by $j$; the identity is a closed immersion because its underlying space is the whole closed subset $V$ and its sheaf map is the surjective identity [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] makes $j$ locally of finite type. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], applied to $h$ and $j$, makes $f=j\circ h:Y\to X$ locally of finite type. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives that $Y$ is locally Noetherian. Define $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)=\{y\in Y:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\text{ is regular local}\}$, using the regular-local-ring predicate of [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), proof, first and last paragraphs; Tags 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: The opens $f^{-1}(U_i)$ cover $Y$. For each $y\in Y$, choose $i(y)$ with $f(y)\in U_{i(y)}$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] inside the open $f^{-1}(U_{i(y)})$ to obtain an affine open $W_y$ with $y\in W_y\subseteq f^{-1}(U_{i(y)})$. These $W_y$ cover $Y$. Put $A_y=\mathcal O_X(U_{i(y)})$ and $C_y=\mathcal O_Y(W_y)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the locally finite type morphism $f$ and the actual affine pair $(W_y,U_{i(y)})$. It says that $A_y\to C_y$ is of finite type. No intersection of two affine opens is asserted to be affine, and no finite subcover is needed.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), proof, last paragraph: choose the affine cover V_j mapping into the U_i and apply Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize); Schemes Tag 01IT (schemes.tex, lemma-basis-affine-opens).

proof.text: The ring $A_y$ is J-2 by hypothesis. Hence [def-exc-excellent-ring], applied to the finite type $A_y$-algebra $C_y$, says that the set $E_y=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}C_y:(C_y)_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open. Under the canonical affine identification of $W_y$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C_y$, let $O_y\subseteq W_y$ correspond to $E_y$. For $z\in W_y$, clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], with ambient scheme $Y$ and affine open $W_y$, gives $(C_y)_{\mathfrak q_z}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,z}$. Regular locality is unchanged by this ring isomorphism directly from [def-weil-regular-scheme]: an isomorphism identifies the maximal ideals and their generating sets, the ideals witnessing Noetherianity, and the prime chains measuring Krull dimension. Thus $z\in O_y$ if and only if $z\in\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$, so $O_y=W_y\cap\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$. The set $O_y$ is open in $Y$ because it is open in the open subset $W_y$. Since the $W_y$ cover, $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)=\bigcup_{y\in Y}O_y$ is open in $Y$. For empty $Y$ this is the empty union and is open as well.

source.place: Tag 07R4 (lemma-J), proof, last paragraph, Reg(Y) intersect V_j = Reg(V_j); ring predicate: More on Algebra Tag 07P7 (more-algebra.tex, definition-J); stalk comparison: Schemes Tag 01HV (schemes.tex, lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6).

proof.text: Apply clause (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] once more to the whole affine open $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $Y$. Its local ring at a prime $\mathfrak q$ is $B_{\mathfrak q}$, so the open subset $\operatorname{Reg}(Y)$ just proved open is exactly the ring regular locus of $B$; the same direct invariance of regular locality under isomorphism uses [def-weil-regular-scheme]. We have therefore proved openness of the regular locus for every finite type $R$-algebra $B$. This is precisely the J-2 predicate of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Since $V$ was arbitrary, every affine open has a J-2 coordinate ring, as required.
